newsitem.title: USA: Study says 35 percent of U.S. households own guns.
newsitem.headline: Study says 35 percent of U.S. households own guns.

text.p: A Justice Department survey released on Monday found that 35 percent of all U.S. households owned guns and more than half of all privately owned firearms were stored unlocked.

The department's research arm, the National Institute of Justice, reported that 44 million Americans in 1994 owned 192 million firearms, including 65 million handguns, a total lower than in previous studies.

It said 74 percent of the gun owners possessed at least two firearms, primarily for crime protection, while 68 percent of the handgun owners also had at least one shotgun or rifle in their private collection.
The study said on a typical day in the United States 1 million adults carry a gun with them and a further 2 million carry a firearm in their vehicle.
The survey, which was carried out by professors from Georgetown and Ducke, said protection represented the main reason that nearly half of all gun owners possessed a firearm.
It found that 20 percent of all gun-owning households had an unlocked and loaded gun. The report cited the accidental shooting deaths of 185 children in 1994.

Middle-aged, college-educated people in small rural towns were most likely to own guns, according to the survey of more than 2,500 adults. Also, 42 percent of men, but only 9 percent of the women, surveyed owned firearms.
About 80 percent of the gun owners reported that their parents kept a gun in the house while they were growing up.
"This report paints a more detailed picture of the varieties of gun ownership in this country," Jeremy Travis, the director of the agency, said in a statement.
